name: OpenRappter Training
tagline: Run the command. Read what it actually printed. Eight modules built only from things that were run.
_note: Every entry here is a live entry with card scenes and no video file, on purpose. Nothing points at a media file that does not exist. Posters are inline SVG data URIs so the channel ships zero binary assets. The full description under each entry is the lesson — it is written to be followed without ever pressing play. Screen capture is planned, not done: CONTENT_PLAN.md sits next to this file and lists exactly what still needs recording, module by module, plus the constraints any capture has to satisfy. That plan is the only aspirational document in this directory and it says so at the top.
_why_no_app_scenes: RAPP Vision live scenes drive a real app in an iframe. OpenRappter's two interactive web surfaces cannot be driven this way: openrappter/index.html opens a WebSocket to ws://<host>:18790 (line 309) and openrappter/dojo.html defaults its gateway field to ws://127.0.0.1:18790 (line 76). Both need a gateway running on the VIEWER's machine, which a hosted page cannot assume. The remaining web surfaces (docs/tutorial.html, docs/architecture.html, docs/docs.html) are static prose with nothing to drive, and docs/agent-dashboard.html cross-origin-fetches raw.githubusercontent.com. So no scene in this channel loads an app. That is a deliberate refusal, not an omission.

videos.title: Module 1 — Install OpenRappter and prove it is running (no pip install required)
videos.description:
You have a machine and five minutes. The goal is not a green install message — it is a runtime you have watched answer.

THE FASTEST VERIFIABLE PATH — zero dependencies:

    git clone https://github.com/kody-w/openrappter.git
    cd openrappter/python
    python3 -m openrappter.cli --status
    python3 -m openrappter.cli --list-agents

Both commands run on a clean clone with nothing pip-installed. `--status` prints `agents_loaded: 17`. `--list-agents` prints all seventeen with descriptions: ContextMemory, Watchmaker, ComputerUse, SelfHealingCron, Phone, Pong, ManageMemory, CodeReview, LearnNew, Pokemon, HackerNews, Pipeline, Git, Twin, Web, DemoRecorder, Shell.

READ THE WARNING, DO NOT HIDE IT. Both commands also emit:

    WARNING: Failed to load .../google_voice_agent.py: No module named 'agents'

There are 18 agent files in `python/openrappter/agents/` (19 `*_agent.py` files, one of which is the `basic_agent.py` base class) and 17 of them load. That is real on main at commit d314ba7, and it is the first honest lesson of the course: the runtime tells you what it could not do and expects you to read it. Module 4 shows the same file loading cleanly under a different loader, and Module 5 shows the two-line import guard that is the whole difference.

THE ONE STATUS FIELD THAT SHAPES YOUR CURRICULUM. `--status` reports `"copilot_available": false` on any machine without an authenticated GitHub Copilot CLI. That is fine, and you should not go fix it yet. Modules 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 all work anyway — they are deterministic Python. Only natural-language routing and the `/chat` endpoint need Copilot.

OPTIONAL FULL INSTALL. From `python/`, `pip install .` adds the `openrappter` console command — `python/pyproject.toml` declares `[project.scripts] openrappter = "openrappter.cli:main"` — and the aiohttp-backed gateway. Declared dependencies are pyyaml>=6.0, requests>=2.28 and aiohttp>=3.13. You do not need any of it for the next six modules.

WHAT THE CLI ACTUALLY OFFERS. The authoritative option list is the argparse block in `python/openrappter/cli.py` (around lines 694-714): `--version`, `--task/-t`, `--status/-s`, `--list-agents/-l`, `--exec/-e` (which takes exactly two values, AGENT and QUERY), and the gateway family `--gateway`, `--gateway-host`, `--gateway-port` (default 18790), `--gateway-token`, `--gateway-trusted-origin` — plus a set of `clawhub` subcommands. If a tutorial hands you a flag that is not in that block, the tutorial is stale. Module 5 names two such flags by their exact error text.

THE ONE-LINER, AND WHY THIS COURSE WILL NOT RUN IT FOR YOU. The README publishes `curl -fsSL https://kody-w.github.io/openrappter/install.sh | bash`. Read install.sh before you pipe it to a shell: it clones into `$HOME/.openrappter` (backing up any non-git directory it finds sitting there), runs `npm install`, runs `npm run build`, and puts `openrappter` on your PATH. That is a lot of machine to hand over on faith.

VERIFICATION STATUS: PARTIALLY VERIFIED. The manual Python path above was exercised on a clean clone at commit d314ba7. The curl one-liner was NOT executed — only read — because running it would have overwritten a real `~/.openrappter` on the verifying machine. Treat the one-liner as documented-but-unexercised here, and see Module 8 for the rest of the honest map.

videos.title: Module 2 — Give an AI a memory file you own (no API key, no cloud)
videos.description:
The use case: an assistant that remembers facts about your work across sessions, where the memory is a file on your disk that you can read, diff, back up or delete.

STORE A FACT:

    python3 -m openrappter.cli --exec ManageMemory "the deploy command is npm run deploy"

Returns `{"status": "success", "message": "Stored fact memory: ...", "memory_id": "e8fb5fda-5d0"}`.

RECALL IT:

    python3 -m openrappter.cli --exec ContextMemory "deploy"

Returns `Found 1 memories matching: deploy`, a formatted line, and a `familiar: true` flag.

NOW DO IT IN ENGLISH — WITH NO MODEL RUNNING:

    python3 -m openrappter.cli --task "remember that Python works"

This works with `copilot_available: false`, and the reason matters more than the trick. `Orchestrator._fallback_response()` in `python/openrappter/cli.py` (around line 550) holds a literal keyword table: remember/store/save/memorize/note that → ManageMemory; recall/remind me/what do you know → ContextMemory; run/execute/bash/ls/cat → Shell; learn/create agent/teach → LearnNew. Anything unmatched is scored against every loaded agent's description. It is a router, not a model. Deterministic, offline, and easy to reason about when it picks wrong.

OPEN THE FILE:

    cat ~/.openrappter/memory.json

Each entry carries id, message, theme, importance, tags, date, time, accessed, sensitivity, and a `trust` block with custodians, subjects and origin_audience. That is the real schema. Read it once and you will never wonder where your data went.

DOC CORRECTION #1 — the schema in the docs is stale. `skills.md` section 9 shows memory entries keyed `mem_1707100000000` carrying only message/theme/timestamp. The runtime writes a much richer record keyed by a short uuid. Teach the file, not the doc.

DOC CORRECTION #2 — and this one will actually bite you. `skills.md` lists `OPENRAPPTER_HOME` in its environment table as "Data directory for config, memory, skills." The memory agents do not read it. `manage_memory_agent.py:102` and `context_memory_agent.py:76` both hardcode `Path.home() / ".openrappter"`. The only module in the Python package that honours `OPENRAPPTER_HOME` is `brainstem.py:59`. If you want your memory somewhere else, you must override `HOME` for the process — setting `OPENRAPPTER_HOME` will silently do nothing to your memory file.

WHY THIS IS THE SECOND MODULE. It is the shortest honest path from "I cloned a repo" to "an AI runtime is holding my data, on my disk, in a format I can read." No key, no account, no network call.

VERIFICATION STATUS: VERIFIED. Store, recall, the natural-language fallback and the on-disk schema were all exercised live at commit d314ba7. Both doc corrections were confirmed by reading the source lines cited above.

videos.title: Module 3 — Real work with zero AI: Shell, CodeReview, Git (and the --exec trap)
videos.description:
This is the module for anyone who says "show me it doing something useful before I buy a Copilot subscription" — and it is also the honest answer to "what does this thing do when the model is down?"

START WITH THE GOTCHA, BECAUSE IT COSTS EVERYONE AN HOUR. `--exec <Agent> <query>` passes your string as `query=` and nothing else. `python/openrappter/cli.py:885-887` is three lines long:

    if args.exec:
        agent_name, query = args.exec
        result = orchestrator.execute_agent(agent_name, query=query)

ShellAgent survives that because its `perform()` calls `_parse_query()` to infer an action from the string. Agents whose metadata declares an `action` enum do not. So:

    python3 -m openrappter.cli --exec Git "status"
    → {"status": "error", "message": "No action specified..."}

Same for CodeReview, Pipeline and Web. Nothing is broken; the CLI simply has no way to send a second parameter.

WHAT DOES WORK FROM THE CLI:

    python3 -m openrappter.cli --exec Shell "ls"
    → {"status": "success", "path": ".", "items": [...], "count": 5}

ShellAgent also handles read, write, list and bash.

SO DRIVE MULTI-ACTION AGENTS FROM PYTHON — it is four lines:

    from openrappter.agents.code_review_agent import CodeReviewAgent
    CodeReviewAgent().execute(
        action="review", file="demo.ts",
        content="const x: any = 1;\nconsole.log(x); // TODO fix\n")

That returns two findings (a todo-comment info and a no-console warning), `"score": 94`, and a `data_slush` block that Module 7 turns into a pipeline.

    from openrappter.agents.git_agent import GitAgent
    GitAgent().execute(action="status")

returns the porcelain status of whatever repository the process's working directory is in, as structured JSON. The cwd is the repo it acts on — there is no `--repo` flag.

THE DISCOVERY COMMAND — point at the contract, not the prose. Every agent's own metadata is the truth about what it can do:

    python3 -c "from openrappter.agents.git_agent import GitAgent; import json; print(json.dumps(GitAgent().metadata, indent=1))"

`metadata['parameters']['properties']['action']['enum']` is the list. Git is status/diff/log/branch/commit/pr. CodeReview is review/suggest/diff_review. Learn that one command and you never need a doc for an agent again.

DO NOT COPY THESE FROM THE README. `openrappter --exec Update "check"` and `--exec DailyTip "preview"` will not work in Python. Update, DailyTip, Dream, TTS, Browser and Ouroboros exist only under `typescript/src/agents/`; they are not in `python/openrappter/agents/`. Module 8 covers which runtime to pick for which job.

VERIFICATION STATUS: VERIFIED. The Shell run, the CodeReview score of 94, the GitAgent porcelain status, and the exact `No action specified` error from `--exec Git "status"` were all exercised live at commit d314ba7. The action enums and the three-line exec branch were confirmed by reading the source.

videos.title: Module 4 — Run the brainstem: one local HTTP endpoint, and hot-load an agent into it
videos.description:
The use case: one local service on your machine that a web UI, a shell script, another AI or a teammate's tool can all call — and the ability to add a capability to it without restarting anything.

START IT (stdlib only, works on an un-pip-installed clone):

    cd openrappter/python
    PORT=7099 python3 -m openrappter.brainstem

The default port is 7072. `brainstem.py:62` reads `PORT`, then `OPENRAPPTER_BRAINSTEM_PORT`, then falls back to 7072. Set `PORT=7071` and it drops in exactly where a RAPP brainstem sits.

READ ITS HEALTH:

    curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7099/health

Returns status, version 1.10.0, the agent list, brainstem_dir, the soul path, the model (`claude-sonnet-5` by default, per `MODEL` at brainstem.py:63) and a `copilot` flag. `/agents`, `/version`, `/models` and `/login/status` all answer too.

THE DETAIL WORTH STOPPING ON. The brainstem loads 18 agents — including `GoogleVoice`, the one the CLI could not load back in Module 1. Same files on disk, different loader. The brainstem installs kernel-parity import shims that alias `agents.basic_agent` to OpenRappter's own BasicAgent, and that alias is the entire difference. Module 5 shows you how to write an agent that never depends on which loader picked it up.

THE HOT DROP-IN — this is the payoff. Write a `hello_agent.py`, then:

    curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7099/agents/import -F "file=@hello_agent.py"
    → {"status": "ok", "message": "Agent hello_agent.py imported successfully."}

The next `/health` lists `Hello` among the agents. No restart, no build step, no plugin manifest. That is what "UI is optional" means in practice: the capability surface grows over HTTP.

THE /chat ENVELOPE, AND ITS HONEST LIMIT:

    curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7099/chat -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d '{"message":"hello"}'

Without an authenticated Copilot you get the documented error envelope: `{"schema":"rapp-chat/1.0","status":"error","error":"Copilot not authenticated — set GITHUB_TOKEN or run `gh auth login`","session_id":"..."}`. The contract lives in `contracts/rapp-chat-v1.json`: a request requires `message` (with `user_input`, `sessionId` and `history` accepted as legacy aliases); a success response requires schema, status, response, content and session_id. Note that the answer comes back in the field named `response` — that is the frozen behaviour every RAPP-shaped client depends on.

WHAT THIS MODULE DOES NOT SHOW YOU, AND WHY. An authenticated `/chat` tool loop — Copilot choosing a tool, the agent running, the result landing in `response` — was never observed. `copilot_available` was false throughout verification, and the repo's own ROADMAP still lists "Interactive login verified end-to-end in a browser" as an unchecked item. That step needs a human at a keyboard. Say so out loud rather than filming a mock.

AND A DELIBERATE OMISSION: this channel never scripts OpenRappter's web UI. `openrappter/index.html` opens a WebSocket to `ws://<host>:18790` and `openrappter/dojo.html` defaults its gateway field to `ws://127.0.0.1:18790`. Both require a gateway running on the viewer's own machine, so a hosted page cannot honestly demonstrate them. If you want the dashboard, start the gateway yourself first.

VERIFICATION STATUS: PARTIALLY VERIFIED. The brainstem start, `/health`, `/agents`, `/version`, `/models`, `/login/status`, the `POST /agents/import` hot drop-in end-to-end, and the unauthenticated `/chat` error envelope were all exercised live at commit d314ba7. `python/tests/test_openrappter_brainstem.py` holds 23 wire-parity tests and passed locally in 6.2s. The authenticated `/chat` tool loop is UNVERIFIED.

videos.title: Module 5 — Write your own agent: one file, live in one request
videos.description:
The use case: the built-in agents do not do your job, you want to add one, and you do not want a plugin system, a YAML file or a build step.

WRITE ONE FILE. A class extending BasicAgent. `self.name` is the name it registers under. `self.metadata` is OpenAI-tools shape — name, description, parameters. `perform(self, **kwargs)` does the work.

MAKE IT PORTABLE THE WAY THE CODEBASE DOES. Copy the guarded import from `python/openrappter/agents/twin_agent.py:33-36` verbatim:

    try:  # grail brainstem
        from agents.basic_agent import BasicAgent
    except ImportError:  # openrappter's python package
        from openrappter.agents.basic_agent import BasicAgent

Those four lines are why the same file loads under the CLI, under the brainstem, and under a bare RAPP kernel. `docs/RAPP.md` explains the reasoning and check R7 enforces it. It is also, incidentally, exactly what `google_voice_agent.py` is missing — which is why it fails in Module 1 and succeeds in Module 4.

ADD A MANIFEST NOW, NOT LATER. Six lines at module level:

    __manifest__ = {
        "schema": "rapp-agent/1.0",
        "name": "@yourscope/your-slug",
        "version": "1.0.0",
        "description": "...",
        "capabilities": ["filesystem-read"],
    }

That is what Module 6's gate checks. Six lines now versus a rewrite later.

LOAD IT — two ways, both verified. Copy the file into `python/openrappter/agents/` and it is hot-loaded with no build; or POST it to a running brainstem with `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7099/agents/import -F "file=@my_agent.py"`.

READ THE ENRICHED CONTEXT. Inside `perform()`, `self.get_signal('temporal.time_of_day')` returned `'night'` and `self.get_signal('orientation.confidence')` returned `'low'` in a live run. Those signals are injected by `slosh()` (basic_agent.py:221) before `perform()` is ever called — you do not wire anything up.

EMIT DOWNSTREAM SIGNAL. Return a `data_slush` key in your JSON and the framework extracts it into `self.last_data_slush` (basic_agent.py:147-151 and 173). That is the input to Module 7, where two agents hand off state with no model in between.

RETURN TYPE — the docs disagree, so here is the rule. README and skills.md say return a JSON string; `docs/tutorial.html` returns a plain dict. Both work in Python — a dict return was verified and its `data_slush` was still extracted. Teach the JSON string as the contract, because that is what the tool loop expects, and mention that a dict happens to work.

DO NOT COPY THESE TWO LINES FROM tutorial.html — both are verified broken. `openrappter --agent greeter "greet Alice"` fails because there is no `--agent` flag; argparse errors with `invalid choice: 'greeter'`. `openrappter --exec ShellAgent "read package.json"` returns `Agent 'ShellAgent' not found` — the registered name is `Shell`, not `ShellAgent`. The same tutorial page still brands itself v1.9.1 and says "Available agents (3)"; the repo is 1.10.0 and loads 17. Use `--list-agents` as the source of truth.

VERIFICATION STATUS: VERIFIED. A hand-written `hello_agent.py` was imported into a running brainstem and appeared in the next `/health`. The signal reads, the dict-return behaviour and the two broken tutorial commands were all exercised live at commit d314ba7.

videos.title: Module 6 — Make your agent adoptable: run the RAPP conformance gate and read it red
videos.description:
The use case: you wrote an agent. Will a governed enterprise deployment actually accept it, or will it be silently withheld?

RUN THE GATE:

    cd openrappter
    python3 conformance.py

On main at commit d314ba7 with a clean tree, the result is **4 passed, 4 failed, 1 skipped**. Film that. Do not film a green screenshot you did not produce — reading a real gate red is the actual skill this module teaches.

WHAT PASSES. R1: every agent is a single file, in every language — 48 of them, 18 Python and 30 TypeScript/JavaScript. R6: the brainstem keeps wire parity with the RAPP kernel — /chat, /health, /version, /agents and /models are all present, and /chat replies in the field named `response`. R7: no agent hard-imports kernel internals. R8: the RAPP substrate is attributed in the README.

WHAT FAILS, EXACTLY. R2 and R3: `google_voice_agent.py` and `GoogleVoiceAgent.ts` carry no `rapp-agent/1.0` manifest at all — the same file that would not load in Module 1, failing a second way. R4: `twin_agent.py` under-declares `credential-access`, and the evidence the checker cites is its own `os.environ.get` call. R5: `phone_agent.py` claims `credential-access` and `network-access` it never reaches, and `twin_agent.py` claims an unused `filesystem-read`.

R9 SKIPS UNLESS YOU INSTALL THE BROKER. The credential scan shells out to `rapp-keyring`; without it on PATH, `conformance.py` returns a SKIP rather than passing silently (see conformance.py:365-370). Install it with `curl -fsSL https://kody-w.github.io/rapp-keyring/install.sh | bash` and re-run. A skip is honest. A quiet pass would not be.

WHY R4 IS THE LOAD-BEARING CHECK. `docs/RAPP.md` makes the argument plainly: every agent's capability list is produced by reading that agent's own syntax tree, not by a human deciding what sounded right — and the same analysis runs at approval time and again at load time in the enterprise strain, `kody-w/rapp-light`. An agent that under-declares is refused there. R5 is the opposite failure and it is a slower poison: a false `process-exec` claim gets you withheld by an organisation that forbids it, for capability you never actually use.

THIS IS A LIVE CI SIGNAL, NOT DECORATION. `.github/workflows/rapp-conformance.yml` runs `python3 conformance.py` un-suppressed on push and pull request; the `continue-on-error` is only on the rapp-keyring install step, and `|| true` only on the artifact report. Use `python3 conformance.py --json` for your own CI.

THE EXERCISE. Run the gate against the agent you wrote in Module 5 and make it green. That is the module — not watching someone else's repo pass.

VERIFICATION STATUS: VERIFIED. The 4/4/1 result and the exact R2/R3/R4/R5 failures were produced by a live run on a clean checkout of main at d314ba7. The nine checks, the capability-evidence table and the CI gating step were confirmed by reading conformance.py and the workflow. videos.title: Module 7 — Chain agents with no LLM in the middle: data_slush, AgentChain, Pipeline
videos.description:
The use case: multi-agent workflows that are cheap, fast, testable and produce the same answer twice — instead of a model improvising your control flow.

LEVEL 1 — MANUAL HANDOFF. Agent A returns `"data_slush": {"source_agent": "A", "temp_f": 65}`. Then:

    b.execute(query="...", upstream_slush=a.last_data_slush)

Inside B, `self.context['upstream_slush']` holds A's signals. In a live run B saw `{"source_agent": "A", "temp_f": 65, "condition": "cloudy"}` exactly. The plumbing is `basic_agent.py:134-136` (pop `upstream_slush`, put it in context) and `:147-151` (extract the returned `data_slush`).

LEVEL 2 — AgentChain, WITH AUTOMATIC FORWARDING:

    from openrappter.agents.chain import AgentChain
    ch = AgentChain()
    ch.add_step("first", a).add_step("second", b)
    r = ch.run({"query": "go"})

`r.status == 'success'`, step 2 saw step 1's slush without you passing it, and `r.final_slush` is step 2's.

CORRECT THE OBVIOUS WRONG GUESS. The constructor takes an OPTIONS dict, not a list of agents. `AgentChain([a, b])` raises `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'`, because `__init__(self, options=None)` immediately calls `options.get('stop_on_error', True)`. Use `AgentChain()` and then `.add_step()`. Neither the README nor skills.md documents this signature — you would only find it by reading `chain.py:49`.

LEVEL 3 — DECLARATIVE PIPELINE WITH PARALLEL FAN-OUT:

    PipelineAgent(agent_resolver=lambda n: pool.get(n))
    p.execute(action="validate", spec=SPEC)
    p.execute(action="run", spec=SPEC)

THE STEP SCHEMA IS DOCUMENTED NOWHERE, so learn it here. Every step needs BOTH an `id` and a `type`. `type` is one of `agent`, `parallel`, `conditional`, `loop` (the dispatch is `pipeline_agent.py:174-185`). An `agent` step takes `agent`; a `parallel` step takes `agents: [...]`. Omit either field and `validate` returns `"Each step must have an id"` and `"type is required"` — which is the first wall everybody hits.

A SPEC THAT VERIFIABLY WORKS:

    {"name": "demo",
     "steps": [{"id": "s1", "type": "agent", "agent": "A"},
               {"id": "s2", "type": "parallel", "agents": ["B", "C"]}],
     "input": {"query": "go"}}

`validate` returns `valid: true, stepCount: 2`; `run` returns `status: completed` — and both parallel branches received s1's data_slush as their upstream.

WHERE THIS PAYS OFF. Cron jobs, sub-agent chains and broadcast fallbacks where live context should flow between agents without a model interpreting in between, and where you want a unit test instead of a vibe check. If you want to go further, `python/openrappter/agents/` also ships broadcast.py (BroadcastManager), router.py (AgentRouter), subagent.py (SubAgentManager) and graph.py (AgentGraph), all importable.

VERIFICATION STATUS: VERIFIED. The manual A→B handoff, the two-step AgentChain with automatic forwarding, the `AgentChain([a, b])` AttributeError, and the Pipeline validate-then-run with parallel fan-out were all exercised live at commit d314ba7. The constructor signature and step dispatch were confirmed by reading chain.py and pipeline_agent.py.

videos.title: Module 8 — Read the map before you bet: what is proven, what is partial, what is fiction
videos.description:
"I like this. Can I build my team's workflow on it?" The answer is genuinely yes for some things and genuinely no for others, and a training channel that will not say which is worse than no channel.

RUN THE TESTS YOURSELF — AND USE THIS EXACT FLAG:

    cd openrappter/python
    python3 -m pytest tests -q --continue-on-collection-errors

Without `--continue-on-collection-errors` you get NO test run at all. The bare `python3 -m pytest tests -q` on a clean clone ends in `!!!!!!! Interrupted: 7 errors during collection !!!!!!!` / `7 errors in 8.07s` — pytest aborts before executing a single test, because seven test modules import `aiohttp` at module scope. Do not read that as a broken project and do not read it as a passing one; it is a collection abort, and the flag is how you get past it.

With the flag, on a clone with NOTHING installed, the summary line is verbatim:

    9 failed, 900 passed, 1 skipped, 7 errors, 51 subtests passed in 18.57s

(The wall-clock figure moves run to run; the counts did not.) That is 52 test files under `tests/`. The 7 collection errors and the 9 failures are the SAME gap — every one of them is `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'aiohttp'` in the gateway, channels and providers modules. `python/pyproject.toml` line 17 declares `aiohttp>=3.13` as a hard runtime dependency, so `pip install .` should supply it — that install was NOT run here, so treat the clean-run claim as the manifest's, not a measurement. What WAS measured is the cold state above. That is the honest headline for this whole channel — the deterministic core is heavily tested and passes cold, and the one dependency it is missing is loud about it.

RUNTIME CHOICE, STATED PLAINLY FROM THE PROJECT'S OWN ROADMAP. ROADMAP.md line 13 says: "TypeScript is the primary runtime. Python is ~60% complete." Its parity table gives TypeScript the WebSocket gateway with 60+ RPC methods, a 12-page Lit dashboard, 22 channels, 5 providers, the plugin system and the Rappter Manager — all marked TS-only. Pick TypeScript for the dashboard and channel story. Pick Python for single-file agents, the brainstem and conformance, which is exactly what Modules 1-7 taught you.

THE SPINE'S VERDICT, QUOTED NOT PARAPHRASED. The RAPP spine lists OpenRappter as a "consumer substrate-distro; parity target incomplete" and says current releases are "a parity target, not yet a conformant replacement for the reference kernel." Its protocol entry `protocol:kody-w/openrappter/entry` sits in the spine's unresolved required-material list. That is ambition with a scoreboard attached, which is a better thing to hand a learner than a claim.

THE VERIFY-DO-NOT-TRUST EXERCISE. Four sources disagree about how many Python agents there are. The README's Python table lists five (Shell, ManageMemory, ContextMemory, LearnNew, Pokemon). skills.md tells you to "expect agents_loaded: 7". ROADMAP's parity table says 13. The live answer is 17 loaded from 18 files on disk. Docs also disagree on tests: ROADMAP.md line 33 says "126 across 37 files" for Python; the actual tree has 52 test files and runs 900 passing tests. The command beats every document, every time. That is the habit this course is really teaching.

PROMPTS.md IS NOT CURRICULUM — SAY IT OUT LOUD. Its 40 entries — "The Lazarus Protocol" (agents that resurrect themselves), "The Parliament" (self-governing agent democracy), "Darwin's Colosseum", "The Consciousness Test" — are design fiction written as prose. They name TypeScript agents in sentences; nothing in the repo executes them as written. Read them as a vision document. Do not treat any of them as a getting-started guide, and do not build a module on them. This channel deliberately does not.

SAFETY POSTURE, FROM THE PROJECT'S OWN SELF-AUDIT. `docs/RAI_AUDIT.md` classifies OpenRappter as a "higher-risk developer tool" — "not because of a sensitive domain, but because it grants an LLM autonomous local code execution" — and names the dual-use shell + codegen surface as the load-bearing risk. Its own top-8 must-fix list still includes first-run capability consent, a stricter default approval policy for curl/wget/pip/npm/chmod, and an approval gate on LearnNewAgent-generated code before it loads. Anyone pointing this at a work machine deserves to hear that sentence before they install.

THE ONE-MINUTE TRUST CHECK to leave with:

    python3 -m openrappter.cli --status      # what actually loaded
    python3 conformance.py                   # is the agent contract green
    python3 -m pytest tests -q --continue-on-collection-errors   # does the core still pass

Three commands, no opinions. The flag on the third one is not optional on a clean clone — without it pytest aborts at collection and runs nothing.

VERIFICATION STATUS: VERIFIED for everything stated above, at commit d314ba7 — the test run is a live result, and every quoted line was read in the file it is attributed to. Explicitly NOT verified anywhere in this channel: the whole TypeScript runtime (node_modules and dist are both absent from the clone, so nothing was built or run — every TS claim above is the ROADMAP's, not a measurement), the curl one-liner installer, `quickstart.sh`, the authenticated Copilot `/chat` loop, LearnNewAgent's generation quality, RappterHub/ClawHub registry install and search, the Python WebSocket gateway, the macOS menu-bar app, and every agent needing hardware, a ROM, or the network (Pokemon, Phone, GoogleVoice, ComputerUse, DemoRecorder, Web, HackerNews, Watchmaker, SelfHealingCron, Twin).
